subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error warning delivery policy beyond the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` boolean, and what should happen by default when a side-effecting tool fails but the final reply sounds successful?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config and failed-side-effect safety semantics, so source inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose the user-facing product contract safely.

options.title: Add Explicit Delivery Policy
options.body: Add an opt-in enum that preserves current safety by default while allowing hosted or group-chat operators to choose final-only or off behavior with docs and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep Existing Boolean Only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported all-off operator control and close or defer the success-aware enum request after documenting that contract.

options.title: Move To Channel-Specific Policy
options.body: Put the success-aware suppression behavior under Telegram, Discord, or team-chat channel configuration instead of adding another global messages key.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Delivery Policy
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in enum that preserves current safety by default while allowing hosted or group-chat operators to choose final-only or off behavior with docs and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent source and merged-history signal on the warning-policy and message-delivery paths.
